phases.name: Separate the two ingestion modes
phases.description: Start with source diversity, then distinguish low-latency event ingestion from durable batch-file staging.

phases.name: Transform with explicit correctness boundaries
phases.description: Use one managed Beam processing layer for streaming and batch while making failure isolation, analytical storage, and operations visible.

phases.name: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
phases.description: Connect source and sink paths, then explain event time, late data, idempotency, retries, and monitoring.

phases.name: Validate targets and assumptions

steps.phase: Separate the two ingestion modes
steps.title: Freeze the exact problem brief
steps.content:
Title: Build a Big Data Processing Pipeline
Description: Design a batch and streaming data pipeline that processes data transformations, handles both real-time and batch workloads, and stores results for analytics.
Requirements:
1. Ingest data from various sources
2. Process batch and streaming data
3. Transform and enrich data
4. Load data into data warehouse
5. Handle late data and watermarks
6. Implement windowing strategies
7. Monitor pipeline performance
8. Handle pipeline failures
Constraints:
1. Processing latency under 10 seconds
2. Support 1TB+ daily data volume
3. Ensure exactly-once semantics
4. Auto-scale workers dynamically
5. Cost-effective resource usage
Hints:
1. Dataflow for Apache Beam pipelines
2. Pub/Sub for message ingestion
3. BigQuery for data warehousing
4. Cloud Storage for staging
5. Dataflow templates for reusability
6. Cloud Monitoring for metrics

steps.phase: Separate the two ingestion modes
steps.title: Represent independent batch and event producers
steps.content: Model external databases, APIs, and files as source systems without assuming their count, schema, arrival pattern, or delivery guarantees. Give each source a stable event or record identity where the upstream can provide one.

component.label: Source Systems and Exporters
component.description: Producers of event records and scheduled batch extracts.

properties.purpose: Represent heterogeneous databases, APIs, and file producers; source-specific schemas, volume mix, and delivery guarantees are not stated, so attach stable source and record identity where available.

component.highlightReason: The pipeline must ingest from various sources, and the brief does not constrain the source technologies.

steps.phase: Separate the two ingestion modes
steps.title: Buffer streaming events with Pub/Sub
steps.content: Use Pub/Sub as the managed event-ingestion boundary so producers do not directly depend on processing workers. Subscription acknowledgement, redelivery, ordering needs, and retention must be selected from event semantics rather than guessed.

component.label: Cloud Pub/Sub Event Ingestion
component.description: Durable decoupling boundary for the streaming event path.

properties.purpose: Buffer and fan out streaming records to Beam consumers; choose ordering keys, acknowledgement behavior, and retention from workload and correctness needs.

component.highlightReason: Pub/Sub is hinted for ingestion and decouples producer bursts from worker availability.

steps.phase: Separate the two ingestion modes
steps.title: Stage batch files durably in Cloud Storage
steps.content: Land batch extracts in a durable object store before processing so jobs can be retried and audited. Use manifests/checksums and immutable object versions where needed; retention and file formats are intentionally left open.

component.label: Cloud Storage Batch Staging
component.description: Durable landing area for batch extracts and replayable inputs.

properties.purpose: Stage batch extracts durably with manifests and integrity metadata so failed jobs can be replayed; format, retention, and partition layout depend on source contracts.

component.highlightReason: Cloud Storage is hinted for staging and creates a replayable batch boundary separate from live event delivery.

steps.phase: Transform with explicit correctness boundaries
steps.title: Use a managed Beam pipeline for both modes
steps.content: Use Dataflow/Apache Beam transforms for validation, enrichment, event-time processing, and batch execution. Keep source-specific adapters and reusable templates explicit; worker autoscaling is bounded by quotas, hot keys, sink capacity, and cost controls.

component.label: Dataflow / Apache Beam Pipelines
component.description: Managed streaming and batch transformations with event-time semantics.

properties.purpose: Run reusable Beam streaming and batch transforms for validation, enrichment, event-time windows, and late-data handling; scale workers against backlog and sink capacity with budget and quota guardrails.

component.highlightReason: Dataflow is hinted and provides a common processing model while preserving separate streaming and batch inputs.

steps.phase: Transform with explicit correctness boundaries
steps.title: Isolate poison records without losing the pipeline
steps.content: Route records that fail bounded validation or exhaust retry policy into a quarantine/dead-letter queue with failure reason and source identity. Reprocessing must be controlled and idempotent so replay does not silently duplicate warehouse effects.

component.label: Quarantine and Replay Queue
component.description: Failure isolation for invalid or repeatedly failing records.

properties.purpose: Retain records that exhaust processing policy together with source identity and failure reason; authorize controlled replay only after the cause is fixed and sink writes remain idempotent.

component.highlightReason: Failure handling is a requirement; a dead-letter path prevents a few poison records from repeatedly blocking unrelated work.

steps.phase: Transform with explicit correctness boundaries
steps.title: Load curated results into BigQuery
steps.content: Use BigQuery for analytical tables partitioned and clustered according to actual query and retention patterns. Define the event key, deduplication boundary, and publication/commit behavior with the pipeline; do not infer a schema or partition key from the 1TB/day floor.

component.label: BigQuery Analytics Warehouse
component.description: Analytical destination for transformed batch and streaming records.

properties.purpose: Store validated, enriched analytical records from both modes; choose partitioning, clustering, retention, and deduplication keys from query patterns and data contracts.

component.highlightReason: The brief explicitly requires a data warehouse and hints BigQuery as the analytical destination.

steps.phase: Transform with explicit correctness boundaries
steps.title: Observe lag, throughput, correctness, and failure
steps.content: Monitor source backlog, event-time lag, watermark progress, worker utilization, bytes/records processed, sink commit errors, duplicate/replay counts, and dead-letter volume. Set alerts and dashboards around the under-10-second objective and failure recovery.

component.label: Cloud Monitoring Pipeline Telemetry
component.description: Operational signals for freshness, throughput, cost, and recoverability.

properties.purpose: Collect source backlog, event-time lag, watermark progress, worker utilization, throughput, sink errors, duplicate/replay counts, and dead-letter volume for alerting and target evaluation.

component.highlightReason: Pipeline monitoring is explicit and is the evidence needed to validate latency, scale, and failure behavior.

steps.phase: Transform with explicit correctness boundaries
steps.title: Define event time and end-to-end delivery semantics
steps.content: Use event timestamps for event-time windows and watermarks; choose window size, allowed lateness, and correction behavior with the business definition of a late record. Exactly-once is end-to-end only when source identity, processing state, sink commit, retries, and replay are coordinated; a processing engine mode alone cannot guarantee it across arbitrary external side effects.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Send live events to the decoupled topic
steps.content: Publish streaming records with source identity and event time so consumers can process by event time and safely handle redelivery.

connection.label: streaming records with event time
connection.description: Source producers publish identified events to Pub/Sub for buffered processing.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Land batch extracts before asynchronous processing
steps.content: Write batch files and a completion manifest to Cloud Storage; the pipeline should process a completed object once according to an explicit manifest/version identity.

connection.label: extracts and completion manifests
connection.description: Source systems deliver replayable batch inputs and manifests to Cloud Storage staging.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Consume the event stream with Beam
steps.content: Dataflow consumes Pub/Sub subscriptions and checkpoints progress according to the configured processing mode; monitor backlog and event-time lag rather than equating low queue depth with completed output.

connection.label: buffered events to Beam
connection.description: Dataflow reads the streaming subscription and tracks processing progress and event-time watermarks.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Read staged files through the batch pipeline
steps.content: Dataflow processes completed staged objects with reusable batch templates. A retry identifies the same input object/version so writes can be deduplicated or safely replaced.

connection.label: manifest-driven batch jobs
connection.description: Beam batch jobs read immutable staged object versions and process them through the same validated transforms.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Commit validated windowed results to BigQuery
steps.content: Write curated output with stable record keys and a documented sink commit/deduplication strategy. Measure end-to-end event-to-queryable latency against the ten-second target and test late-event corrections.

connection.label: validated windowed results
connection.description: Dataflow commits transformed batch and streaming output into analytical BigQuery tables.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Quarantine records that cannot be processed safely
steps.content: Send validation failures and exhausted retries to the durable quarantine path with enough context for diagnosis, while allowing the main stream to advance when policy permits.

connection.label: failed records and reason
connection.description: Beam routes poison or repeatedly failing records to durable quarantine for controlled remediation.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Replay only after correcting the failure cause
steps.content: A controlled operator or replay job can return corrected records to the same transforms. Preserve original IDs and use idempotent sink behavior to prevent replay from creating duplicate analytical facts.

connection.label: remediated records
connection.description: Authorized replay re-enters the standard Beam validation path with original identity preserved.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Alert on ingestion backlog and delivery health
steps.content: Export subscription backlog, oldest unacknowledged age, publish errors, and redelivery signals so ingestion pressure is visible before freshness degrades.

connection.label: backlog and redelivery signals
connection.description: Pub/Sub delivery metrics feed pipeline freshness and reliability monitoring.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Measure worker scale and event-time progress
steps.content: Track worker autoscaling, transform latency, watermark stalling, throughput, and retries. Use these signals to tune worker bounds and cost controls from measured load.

connection.label: throughput, lag, and worker health
connection.description: Dataflow execution and event-time metrics feed alerting and capacity evaluation.

steps.phase: Connect and reason about delivery semantics
steps.title: Verify sink freshness and analytical load health
steps.content: Observe load job outcomes, queryable freshness, storage growth, and duplicate/correction rates at the warehouse boundary; pipeline completion alone does not prove usable output.

connection.label: load outcomes and freshness
connection.description: BigQuery destination health and output freshness are included in end-to-end pipeline monitoring.

steps.phase: Validate targets and assumptions
steps.title: Prove latency, volume, and cost with representative data
steps.content: The brief specifies under ten seconds and at least 1TB daily but omits the latency percentile, event-size distribution, peak-to-average ratio, source count, retention, schema, window duration, and cost ceiling. Benchmark both modes under peak and recovery load, reconcile input/output counts, inject late and malformed events, and verify worker scaling and replay correctness before claiming the targets.
